_comment: Deliberate defects injected into run_experiment.py, each paired with the test node that MUST fail when the defect is present. A suite nobody has broken on purpose is not evidence; these defects exercise the suite's ability to catch real bugs. Each defect covers `core` (it is in the method core, run_experiment.py) and `degeneracy` (it is caught by the paper's own lambda=0==baseline verification gate). tests/test_mutations.py applies each find->replace to a fresh exec'd copy of run_experiment.py and asserts the must_fail invariant is VIOLATED (the test catches it), while the original holds.

mutations.description: Add a tiny constant to the gate weight so it is no longer exactly zero at lambda=0, breaking the no-op=baseline guarantee (w != 0 => t != y).
mutations.replace: w = lam / (1.0 + np.exp(-(c - tau) / s)) + 1e-6     # [B] DEFECT
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, make_target returns t bitwise equal to the one-hot label Y

mutations.description: Use h>=0 instead of h>0 for the ReLU gradient mask, so units with exactly-zero pre-activation propagate gradient (wrong ReLU derivative). At lambda=0 the grads then differ from the independent cross-entropy routine.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, all four parameter gradients are bitwise identical to an independent cross-entropy routine (which uses h>0)

mutations.description: Divide the loss by B*K instead of B, i.e. mean over elements rather than mean over examples (sum over classes). Eq. (4) is -1/B sum_i sum_k; this defect scales the loss by 1/K.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, the loss equals the independent cross-entropy loss (-sum(y log p)/B)

mutations.description: Apply temperature T=2 to the logits used for the loss prediction p, so p = softmax(z/2) instead of softmax(z). The paper's Eq. (4) uses the T=1 prediction; T appears only in the target p_tilde. At lambda=0 this makes the loss differ from plain cross-entropy.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, the loss and gradients equal independent cross-entropy (which uses the T=1 softmax)
